questions.domain: 1. Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design architectures built for the cloud
questions.question: A fintech team is designing an AWS Step Functions workflow that calls a third-party card processor to capture payments. Some approval paths wait for a human reviewer for several days before the capture step runs. The processor API is not idempotent, so each capture step must run exactly once per execution because a duplicate call would charge the customer twice. The execution must be able to stay open across the multi-day review period. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?

Use a Standard Workflow with an automatic retry on the capture task that resubmits the processor call on each timeout during the execution.
Use an Asynchronous Express Workflow with a callback task token so the processor confirms each capture before the run continues.
Use a Synchronous Express Workflow, which returns the result to the caller and runs the capture step at most once per request.

distractor_rationales: A higher quota adds room that a large enough surge can still consume.
Event source limits slow some batch triggers but do not hold concurrency for the order-capture function.
Provisioned concurrency keeps pre-initialized environments ready, which the team does not want to pay for.
questions.distractor_summary: B limits sources; C is the other concurrency variant; A can still be exhausted.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 Design infrastructure as code
questions.question: An operations team manages a production CloudFormation stack that includes an Amazon RDS DB instance and an Auto Scaling group. A proposed template update changes several resource properties, and a past update replaced a database unexpectedly. Before anything runs, the team must preview how the update would affect each running resource, including any replacement. After approval, CloudFormation must apply the update to the same stack rather than recreate the stack. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?
options: Create a change set for the stack from the updated template, review its resource changes and replacements, and execute it after approval.
Run drift detection on the stack before the update and execute the update directly if no resources show drift from the template.
Update the stack directly with the new template and keep rollback on failure turned on so CloudFormation reverts the stack if an error occurs.
Deploy the updated template as a new stack, test it next to the old stack, and delete the old stack once the new stack works.
questions.correct_rationale: A change set previews how proposed changes affect running resources, including property impacts, and executing it applies the update to the same stack.
distractor_rationales: Drift detection compares resources with the current template, not with the proposed update.
A direct update gives no preview before resources change.
A new stack recreates the environment instead of updating the existing stack.
questions.distractor_summary: C has no preview; D recreates; B checks drift.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 Design infrastructure as code
questions.question: A platform team defines application stacks in the AWS CDK and deploys them from developer laptops with cdk deploy. New stages and stacks are added often, and someone edits the pipeline by hand each time. Deployments must run from a pipeline fed by the source repository instead of from local machines. When engineers add stages or stacks in code, the pipeline must reconfigure itself to deploy them without manual pipeline edits. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?
options: Use CDK Pipelines so the pipeline is defined in the CDK app, keeps itself up to date from the repository, and deploys new stages it finds.
Create a CodePipeline pipeline in the console with a fixed list of deploy actions for each stack and edit it when stacks change.
Run cdk synth in a scheduled CodeBuild project and store the templates in S3 for engineers to deploy from their laptops.
Keep running cdk deploy from laptops and add a CDK aspect that checks the stages and stacks before each local deployment runs.
questions.correct_rationale: A CDK Pipelines pipeline keeps itself up to date from the repository and reconfigures itself to deploy new stages or stacks.
distractor_rationales: A fixed console pipeline needs manual edits when stacks change.
Synthesized templates still get deployed from laptops.
Laptop deployments break the requirement to deploy from a pipeline.
questions.distractor_summary: D stays local; B needs edits; C deploys locally.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 Design CI/CD and DevSecOps pipelines
questions.question: A team's CodePipeline V2 pipeline for a monorepo starts on each push to the main branch of the repository, so documentation edits trigger full production deployments. The pipeline must start for pushes to the release branches and fetch the exact commit that was pushed. Pushes that change nothing outside the docs folder must not start the pipeline. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?
options: Add a push trigger that filters on the release branch names and on file paths excluding the documentation folder, fetching the pushed commit.
Add a push trigger filtered on branch names for the release branches and let each push to those branches start the pipeline.
Turn off change detection and have engineers start the pipeline by hand after reviewing which files each release changes.
Add a push trigger with a file path filter that excludes the docs folder and keep the default start on each push to the main branch.
questions.correct_rationale: Trigger filters start the pipeline on chosen branch names and file paths for a code push and fetch the exact commit.
distractor_rationales: A branch filter alone still starts the pipeline for docs-only pushes.
Manual starts drop the push trigger and its exact-commit fetch.
Keeping the main branch start fails the release branch requirement.
questions.distractor_summary: D keeps main; B lacks a path filter; C is manual.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 Design CI/CD and DevSecOps pipelines
questions.question: A team deploys services on Amazon ECS with the rolling update deployment type. A bad image left a service cycling through failing tasks for an hour before someone noticed. A deployment whose tasks keep failing must be detected and stopped automatically. The service must return to the last deployment in the COMPLETED state without an engineer redeploying it. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?
options: Enable the deployment circuit breaker with the rollback option on the service so a failed deployment rolls back to the last completed deployment.
Enable the deployment circuit breaker on the service without the rollback option so failing deployments are stopped.
Create an EventBridge rule for service deployment events and have an engineer roll back by hand when a failure notice arrives.
Raise the health check grace period on the service so new tasks get more time to start before their health checks count.
questions.correct_rationale: The circuit breaker detects failed deployments, and its rollback option returns the service to the deployment in the COMPLETED state automatically.
distractor_rationales: Without the rollback option, the service does not return to the completed deployment.
A notice plus a manual rollback still needs an engineer to act.
A longer grace period delays detection and does not stop or roll back the deployment.
questions.distractor_summary: C is manual; B has no rollback; D delays detection.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 Design CI/CD and DevSecOps pipelines
questions.question: A fintech company's security policy requires each container image in its private Amazon ECR repositories to carry a cryptographic signature so deployments can verify image origin. Signatures must be produced with AWS Signer and stored with the images in the private repositories. Developers must not run signing tools on their machines or in each build job, and signing should happen automatically on push. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?
options: Use ECR manual signing with the Notation client and AWS Signer plugin in each build job to sign the images before they are pushed.
Turn on Amazon Inspector enhanced scanning for the private repositories so images pushed are scanned automatically for vulnerabilities.
Turn on Amazon ECR managed signing so ECR uses AWS Signer to generate a signature automatically for each image pushed to the repositories.
Turn on tag immutability for the repositories so image tags cannot be overwritten after each image is pushed by a build job.
questions.correct_rationale: ECR integrates with AWS Signer, and managed signing automatically generates cryptographic signatures on push, storing them with images in private repositories.
distractor_rationales: Manual signing runs Notation and the Signer plugin in each build job, which the second requirement rules out.
Vulnerability scanning does not sign images.
Tag immutability prevents overwrites but adds no signature.
questions.distractor_summary: B scans; A signs in builds; D locks tags.

questions.subdomain: 5.3 Design observability and monitoring solutions
questions.question: An e-commerce site's web front end is slow for some shoppers, but synthetic canaries from a few locations show normal page loads. The team cannot reproduce the problem. The team needs page load times and client-side errors collected from actual user sessions in browsers. The data should show the range of affected users, including geolocations and browsers or devices. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?
options: Enable Application Load Balancer access logs and analyze the request processing times recorded for each user's session.
Add more CloudWatch Synthetics canaries in more Regions that load the site's pages on several browsers and record client-side errors.
Add the CloudWatch RUM web client to the site so it reports performance and errors from real visitors' browsers and devices.
Enable AWS X-Ray tracing on the back-end services to find slow downstream calls behind each page request from shoppers.
questions.correct_rationale: CloudWatch RUM collects client-side performance data and errors from actual user sessions and shows user impact by geolocation and browser or device.
distractor_rationales: Load balancer logs show server-side timing, not the browser experience of each user.
More canaries are still synthetic sessions, not actual users.
Back-end traces miss client-side load times and errors.
questions.distractor_summary: B is synthetic; A is server-side; D is back end.

questions.subdomain: 5.3 Design observability and monitoring solutions
questions.question: A healthcare company found patient identifiers and email addresses in application logs in CloudWatch Logs. Support staff query these logs each day with Logs Insights, and subscription filters feed a SIEM. Sensitive data in the log events must be masked wherever the logs are read, including Logs Insights, metric filters and subscription filters. A small group of investigators must still be able to view unmasked values when an incident requires it. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?
options: Leave the log groups unchanged and restrict Logs Insights access with IAM policies so support staff cannot query the sensitive data.
Change the applications to strip identifiers before writing log events so that no unmasked values are stored in CloudWatch Logs.
Encrypt the log groups with a customer managed KMS key and limit decrypt permissions so support staff cannot read log events.
Attach a data protection policy to the log groups with data identifiers for the sensitive types and grant the logs:Unmask permission to the investigators.
questions.correct_rationale: A data protection policy masks matching sensitive data at each egress point, including Logs Insights, metric filters and subscription filters, and users with logs:Unmask can view unmasked data.
distractor_rationales: Restricting queries does not mask data in subscription filters or metric filters.
Stripping identifiers at the source leaves nothing for investigators to unmask.
KMS encryption protects data at rest but does not mask it for readers.
questions.distractor_summary: A restricts without masking; B loses the data; C encrypts at rest.

questions.subdomain: 5.4 Design operational automation and resilient systems
questions.question: An operations team must run a configuration script on several thousand managed instances with AWS Systems Manager. A faulty script once broke a large share of the fleet before anyone stopped it. The command must reach instances gradually, with a limit on how many run it at the same time. The command must stop going to more instances once a set number of instances report errors. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?
options: Use Run Command with a max-concurrency value to limit simultaneous targets and a max-errors value that stops sending at the error threshold.
Use Run Command with a max-concurrency value so a limited number of instances run the script at a time until each instance finishes.
Use Run Command to target the full fleet at the same time and set a max-errors value so it stops sending after the error threshold is reached.
Use a State Manager association for the script so it runs on each instance at the next scheduled association run.
questions.correct_rationale: Run Command concurrency controls limit how many nodes run a command at once, and error controls stop sending the command after the error threshold.
distractor_rationales: Concurrency control alone does not stop the command after errors.
Targeting the full fleet at once is not a gradual rollout.
A State Manager association has no concurrency limit or error threshold in this design.
questions.distractor_summary: C is not gradual; B has no error stop; D has neither control.

questions.subdomain: 5.4 Design operational automation and resilient systems
questions.question: A team rolls out a new AMI to an Auto Scaling group of web servers by terminating instances by hand. Rollouts are slow, and a bad AMI once removed too much capacity. Instances must be replaced in batches while a minimum healthy percentage of capacity stays in service. The rollout must pause after a set percentage of replacements so the team can verify progress before it continues. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?
options: Add a warm pool to the group with the new AMI so pre-initialized instances are ready when old instances are scaled in.
Start an instance refresh with the new launch template version, set the minimum healthy percentage, and add checkpoints at chosen percentages.
Update the launch template and terminate half of the instances at once, then pause to verify progress before terminating the other half of them.
Start an instance refresh with the new launch template version and a minimum healthy percentage and let it run to completion.
questions.correct_rationale: Instance refresh replaces instances in batches based on the minimum healthy percentage, and checkpoints pause after a set percentage of replacements to verify progress.
distractor_rationales: A warm pool speeds scale-out but does not roll out the new AMI in controlled batches.
Terminating half the fleet at once ignores a minimum healthy percentage.
Without checkpoints, the refresh does not pause for verification.
questions.distractor_summary: C ignores healthy capacity; D has no pause; A is not a rollout.

questions.subdomain: 5.4 Design operational automation and resilient systems
questions.question: A small company runs a licensing server on a single Amazon EC2 instance that cannot be clustered. When an underlying host problem occurs, staff must notice the outage and restart the instance by hand. The instance must be restored automatically when AWS detects an underlying hardware or software issue that fails a system status check. The team wants to avoid adding a second server or a load balancer to the design. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?
options: Create a CloudWatch alarm on the instance status check that reboots the instance after the check fails for several minutes.
Use simplified automatic recovery for the instance, or a CloudWatch alarm with a recover action on the system status check.
Run a second licensing server in another Availability Zone behind a Network Load Balancer so traffic moves if one fails.
Create an EBS snapshot of the instance each night and have staff launch a new instance from the latest snapshot after an outage.
questions.correct_rationale: Simplified automatic recovery and CloudWatch action based recovery restore instance availability when AWS detects an underlying hardware or software issue.
distractor_rationales: A reboot on the instance status check does not address an underlying host issue.
A second server behind a load balancer is what the team wants to avoid.
Restoring from a snapshot by hand is neither automatic nor a recovery of the instance.
questions.distractor_summary: D is manual; C adds servers; A reboots on the wrong check.

lessons.domain: 1. Architecture Design and Implementation Built for the Cloud
lessons.title: Designing across accounts, Regions, and networks
body: Professional design questions describe several accounts and Regions and ask which pattern holds up as the estate grows. For event-driven designs, an EventBridge event bus can grant access to an entire organization rather than listing accounts one by one, so new accounts can publish without a policy edit. For very large fan-out work, a Step Functions Map state in Distributed mode sets up large-scale parallel workloads, and an SQS dead-letter queue with maxReceiveCount isolates messages that keep failing so they stop blocking the main queue.

Hybrid and network questions turn on what each connectivity piece actually reaches. A Direct Connect gateway connects to any Region globally, so one set of circuits can serve VPCs in several Regions. Traffic between peered transit gateways needs a static route pointing to the peering attachment, which is a common reason a new peering carries no traffic. PrivateLink lets consumers reach a service from private subnets without internet gateways, NAT, or VPN, and Route 53 Resolver endpoints with conditional forwarding rules resolve DNS between on-premises networks and VPCs.

Data placement questions weigh latency against write patterns. Aurora global database keeps a full copy of data in several locations for low-latency reads by widely separated applications, while every DynamoDB global table replica serves both reads and writes. For generative AI designs, a Bedrock knowledge base searches company data for relevant information at query time, and geographic cross-Region inference keeps processing within geographic boundaries when data residency matters.

lessons.title: Governing many accounts without per-account work
body: Identity questions at this level ask how access scales. One IAM Identity Center permission set, such as Database Admin, can grant access to a list of target accounts, so a role definition is written once. ABAC policies allow an operation when the principal tag matches the resource tag, which avoids a new policy per project. IAM Roles Anywhere issues temporary IAM credentials to workloads that run outside AWS, which replaces long-term access keys on on-premises servers.

Organization policy questions test exactly whom a policy reaches. SCPs do not affect users or roles in the management account, so a guardrail that must bind everyone means workloads belong in member accounts. A resource control policy restricts principals external to the organization from accessing resources in member accounts. The Control Tower Region deny control applies to the landing zone as a whole rather than to one OU, which matters when a scenario needs different Regions for different OUs.

Data protection and audit questions separate retention, visibility, and encryption cost. S3 Object Lock in compliance mode means no user, including the root user, can overwrite or delete a protected object version. Config aggregators replicate data from source accounts and Regions into one account for a read-only view, and conformance packs deploy rules with remediation as one entity across an organization. Multi-Region KMS keys share key material and key ID, so data encrypted in one Region decrypts in another without a cross-Region call, and S3 Bucket Keys reduce the cost of SSE-KMS.

lessons.title: Matching the pricing model to how the workload changes
body: Cost questions usually hide a flexibility requirement. Compute Savings Plans lower prices regardless of instance family, size, OS, tenancy, or Region, which suits a fleet that is expected to modernize or move. For Spot capacity, the price and capacity optimized allocation strategy picks the pools least likely to be interrupted at the lowest possible price, which balances cost against interruption risk better than chasing the lowest price alone.

Data transfer questions reward removing a paid hop. A gateway endpoint gives a VPC access to S3 without an internet gateway or NAT device and at no additional cost, so heavy S3 traffic through a NAT gateway is a common cost leak. When outside parties download large shared datasets, Requester Pays makes the requester rather than the bucket owner pay for requests and data download.

Visibility and storage questions test the mechanics. Both AWS-generated and user-defined cost allocation tags must be activated before they appear in Cost Explorer or cost allocation reports, so tags applied but never activated explain a report with no breakdown. Budget actions can apply an IAM policy, attach an SCP, or target specific EC2 or RDS instances when a threshold is crossed. S3 Intelligent-Tiering moves objects not accessed for 30 days to the Infrequent Access tier, and DynamoDB Standard-IA lowers storage cost where storage dominates the bill.

lessons.title: Moving workloads and keeping them running
body: Migration questions ask which service fits the shape of what is moving. Application Migration Service continuously replicates source servers at block level and converts them for launch on AWS, which suits rehosting whole servers with a short cutover. A DMS task can capture ongoing changes after the initial full load completes, so a database stays in sync until cutover. DataSync automates transfer management and infrastructure for large file and object moves.

Disaster recovery questions weigh cost against recovery speed. Elastic Disaster Recovery recovers applications using affordable storage, minimal compute, and point-in-time recovery, which keeps standby cost low compared with a running copy. Route 53 failover routing responds with the healthy secondary resources when all primary resources are unhealthy, which provides the DNS side of an active-passive design.

Resilience questions test preconditions people forget. An ARC zonal shift moves traffic away from an impaired Availability Zone, but the application must be prescaled so the remaining zones have capacity for the shifted traffic. A Resilience Hub application groups supported resources that are continuously monitored and assessed for resiliency posture, which answers a question about ongoing assessment rather than recovery itself.

lessons.title: Operating a fleet of accounts from the center
body: Deployment questions ask how infrastructure follows organizational change. CloudFormation StackSets can automatically deploy stacks to new accounts when they are added to the target organization or OUs. Drift detection identifies stack resources whose configuration was changed outside CloudFormation, and a stack policy prevents resources from being unintentionally updated or deleted during a stack update.

Release questions test deployment mechanics and checks. With a Network Load Balancer, CodeDeploy supports only the all-at-once configuration for Amazon ECS, so a canary rollout needs another load balancer type. Inspector container image scans can run inside a CI/CD pipeline to report vulnerabilities before deployment, which moves the check ahead of release.

Observability and automation questions favor central views and proactive action. A CloudWatch monitoring account can view and interact with observability data from linked source accounts, and a composite alarm's rule expression references other alarms as children to cut alert noise. Synthetics canaries act like customers, so the experience can be verified with no customer traffic. Systems Manager automations can run across multiple accounts, OUs, and Regions from a central account, and predictive scaling launches capacity ahead of forecasted load rather than reacting to it.
